title: Fast tier tail-latency protection (wait budget + admission control + anti-starvation)
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Implement tail-latency protections for the FAST SLO tier.

Problem:
With more aggressive continuous batching + mixed workloads, FAST tier p99 is sensitive to (a) queueing delay from wait-to-batch and (b) head-of-line blocking when long-prefill requests accumulate. We need explicit FAST-tier protections so “fast” is predictable under concurrency, while still avoiding starvation of long prompts.

Scope:
- Tighter wait budget for FAST tier (time-based cap on queueing before admission/scheduling).
- Admission control for FAST tier under overload (prevent queue blow-ups, preserve p99).
- Starvation prevention so long-prefill requests eventually run even when short requests dominate.

Non-goals:
- Global routing changes (handled by existing smart routing policies).
- Per-tenant auto-tuning of knobs (this is tier-default behavior + safe heuristics).

Owner notes:
This ticket is runtime-side; policy/config surfaces are in ENG-18422/ENG-18430. We should expose enough metrics/reason codes so SRE can validate behavior during canary (ENG-18429/ENG-18426).
acceptance_criteria:
1) FAST tier meets tier SLO gates in benchmark-lab + perf-canary for top model families on target hardware classes (per SLO doc referenced in ENG-18421).
2) Under overload, FAST tier does not exhibit unbounded queue growth: queue depth plateaus via admission control and/or shedding, with explicit reason codes emitted.
3) Anti-starvation: long-prefill requests are not indefinitely deferred by a stream of short requests (validated via mixed prompt-length scenario in perf suite).
4) Streaming: time-to-first-token (TTFT) for FAST tier does not regress beyond the agreed gate (tracked in perf suite and dashboards).
5) Changes are guarded behind tiered-batching feature flag and can be disabled via kill switch (ENG-18431 / PR-28480 dependency satisfied).
implementation_notes:
Implemented FAST-tier protections in scheduler:

A) FAST-tier wait budget
- Add tier-specific max_queue_wait_ms_fast (tighter than standard), applied before joining a batch.
- If wait budget is exceeded, request is forced into next eligible batch (or handled by overload mode if admission cannot occur safely).

B) Admission control / overload mode hooks
- Add per-tier queue depth and in-flight token budget guards.
- When FAST tier is over guardrail, transition to overload behavior:
  - stop increasing batch size for FAST tier (prefer smaller, more frequent batches)
  - optionally shed new FAST-tier requests based on policy (HTTP 429/503 depending on upstream) with clear telemetry
  - emit reason code: overload_admission_block / overload_shed

C) Anti-starvation
- Introduce age-based priority boost: requests accrue “age credits” while queued.
- Add max_defer_count: requests that have been skipped N times are forced eligible.
- Maintain a small reserved prefill slice for long-prefill bucket to guarantee progress (bounded impact to FAST p99 by capping slice).

D) Observability
- FAST-tier metrics tagged by tier with cardinality controls (coordinate with PR-28492 / hotfix PR-28544 if needed).
- Emit tracing span + structured reason code when:
  - wait budget triggered
  - admission blocked/shed
  - starvation prevention forced eligibility

Primary code path: scheduler admission + batch formation loop (prefill/decode balancing).
test_plan:
Perf / correctness validation:
- Unit tests for wait budget + max_defer_count behavior (deterministic queue simulations).
- Integration test with mixed prompt-length buckets (short chat + long summarization) at concurrency ramps.
- Streaming scenario: validate TTFT distribution and chunk cadence at steady-state QPS.
- Overload scenario: verify queue depth plateaus + reason codes emitted; verify system remains responsive (no deadlock/starvation).

Pass/fail:
- Must pass perf suite gates for FAST p99 and TTFT per ENG-18421 thresholds.
- Must show bounded queue depth under synthetic overload (guardrail thresholds documented in rollout checklist).
rollout_plan:
1) Land behind tiered-batching feature flag (ENG-18431).
2) Internal canary in one region + top 1-2 model families.
3) Expand to hosted API subset (small % of FAST-tier traffic) with SRE watching:
   - FAST p99 latency, TTFT
   - queue depth, admission block rate
   - shed rate and customer-visible error rate
4) If stable for 48h and perf-canary remains green, expand to broader hosted.
5) Dedicated remains opt-in pending Dedicated override precedence checks (ENG-18430).

Rollback:
- Flip kill switch to disable FAST-tier protections (revert to standard-tier behavior) OR disable tiered batching entirely depending on symptom.
- If telemetry cost spikes due to tier labels, deploy cardinality hotfix (PR-28544) and temporarily reduce sampling.
comments: 2026-01-16 — Sofia Ivanova: Marking P0. We need explicit FAST-tier protections before we default any batching profiles. Please coordinate with Sean/Aisha on which metrics they need to page on (FAST p99 vs TTFT).

2026-01-22 — Omar El-Sayed: Initial plan: implement max_queue_wait_ms_fast + per-tier admission guardrail based on queue depth and in-flight token budget. For anti-starvation, proposing age-based priority + max defer count rather than hard partitioning queues (keeps utilization decent). Will share graphs after first benchmark run.

2026-02-02 — Marcus Reed: Mixed workload scenario added locally shows head-of-line when long prefill dominates. Suggest we add a cap on “prefill share” for FAST tier to keep decode moving; otherwise TTFT jumps even when p50 looks fine.

2026-02-07 — Omar El-Sayed: Implemented prefill share cap + wait budget. Early results: FAST p99 improved ~12–18% on chat-heavy mix, but saw starvation risk for long-prefill bucket at high QPS. Working on max_defer_count + age credits.
2026-02-13 — Allison Grant: Please ensure reason codes are low-cardinality. We’ve been burned by putting raw thresholds or queue IDs into tags. Prefer enum reason_code + tier label only.

2026-02-18 — Omar El-Sayed: Added starvation prevention (age credits + max_defer_count=3). Verified with synthetic queue test: long-prefill requests complete within bounded time even under continuous short traffic. Next: hook into tracing and expose counters for wait_budget_triggered and forced_eligible_due_to_starvation.

2026-03-03 — Rafael Mendes: For canary, we need explicit abort thresholds (FAST p99 regression, shed rate, error budget). Please add suggested thresholds to the rollout checklist doc once we have baseline numbers.

2026-03-08 — Omar El-Sayed: Opened PR-28458 with wait budget + admission guardrails + anti-starvation. Perf suite: FAST p99 gate passes on A100; borderline on H100 for one model family due to increased context-switching. Adjusted cap values and rerunning.

2026-03-12 — Sofia Ivanova: Reviewed PR. Main ask: clarify overload behavior contract (what errors bubble up) and ensure kill switch disables the whole behavior cleanly. Also confirm streaming TTFT doesn’t regress with max_defer_count logic.

2026-03-15 — Omar El-Sayed: Addressed review. Overload mode now emits reason_code=overload_admission_block and returns standardized upstream signal; kill switch verified. Streaming TTFT stable in benchmarks (no measurable regression within noise).

2026-03-18 — Connor O'Brien: Confirmed included in runtime-1.22 cut. Please coordinate with SRE on canary schedule; release notes will reference “FAST tier tail latency protections” and point to dashboards.
